title: Prefix caching strategy review - Verdant Systems (technical deep dive)
summary: SE-led technical deep dive on prefix/prompt caching strategy for Verdant's multi-tenant LLM service. Covered hit-rate measurement, cache key design, tenant isolation, TTL/eviction policies, effects of batching and quantization, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed on a staged POC: run controlled benchmarks, share recommended config, and review security isolation design.
transcript: [00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro--this is Jared from Redwood AE, with Priya our SE and Carlos on arch. how's everyone doing?
[02:00] Liam: Good, thanks. we are excited to dig into prefix caching — we saw the overview deck, want to validate hit-rate assumptions for our chat product.

[04:00] Priya: Great. i'll kick off with a quick framing: prefix caching = storing model KV state for common prompt prefixes to avoid re-computing the same prefix tokens every request. helps tail latency and cost. note: transcription may say KV cash or K-V cache sometimes in notes, ignore spelling hiccups.

[06:00] Marissa: clarified — in our setup we have multi-tenant sessions, often same prompt wrapper around user message. typical prefix size is 60-120 tokens. we see a lot of reuse for system prompts and company templates.

[08:00] Priya: perfect. two quick metrics we look at: cold latency (no cache) and warm latency (cache hit). also hit-rate by prefix identity and prefix length distribution. example: 65% hit at 40-token prefix in a sample workload is typical for some customers.
[10:00] Ola: question — how do you define the cache key? we are worried about collisions across tenants and accidentally leaking tokens across customers.

[12:00] Priya: good call out. recommended key = tenant_id + model_id + prefix_hash + optional prompt_version. we also suggest salted hashing per-tenant so identical prompts across tenants don't map to same key on shared caches. and include quantization/profile variant in key if using quantized model variant.
[14:00] Ravi: security wise, we need assurance that cached KV blobs can't be read by other tenants, especially in a shared dedicated pool environment.

[16:00] Carlos: there are two patterns: per-tenant cache namespaces (preferred) or encryption-at-rest with KMS keys per-tenant. for in-memory caches the namespace separation + strict RBAC in the shard routing is typical. but we can design a policy where a tenant's salts are applied before keying, which makes accidental cross-tenant key reuse extremely unlikely.
[18:00] Marissa: what about TTLs and eviction? we worry about cache bloat and stale prefix states after prompt updates.

[20:00] Priya: TTL should be driven by observed prompt churn. for static system prompts you can use long TTLs (days), for dynamic user-generated prefixes shorter TTLs (minutes-hours). eviction: LRU with weighted size accounting (since KV cache size varies by sequence length) or segmented LFU for hot prefixes. also include a prompt_version in the key to force invalidation on template changes.
[22:00] Liam: can we do partial prefix caching? e.g., store first N tokens and then stitch with live tokens to reduce memory footprint?

[24:00] Priya: yes — prefix slicing. store fixed-length anchors (say 32-token anchors) for very common starts; on request we replay anchor + remaining tokens. tradeoff: more compute to stitch and maybe lower hit rate for very long shared prefixes. we often combine full-prefix caching for high-frequency templates and anchor caching for noisy prompts.
[26:00] Marissa: how does quantization affect cache validity? our models are 8-bit quantized for cost reasons.

[28:00] Priya: quantization variant must be part of the cache key. also note that some kernel-fusion/kv-layouts differ by quantization and model compilation — so cached KV states produced under one binary/kernel set may not be safe to reuse under another. recommend model_build_id in key plus an ops-version.
[30:00] Ola: batching — if we enable batching to increase throughput, does that interact with prefix caching hit patterns?

[32:00] Carlos: yes, batching can amplify warm path throughput but can also increase observed latencies if you wait to batch. prefix-caches help reduce per-item compute inside the batch. we typically tune max_batch_latency and then rely on caching to keep per-request token compute low so batching windows can be shorter.
[34:00] Liam: curious about measuring hit-rate accurately in production — we need a reliable metric and dashboards.

[36:00] Priya: instrument two metrics: effective_prefix_hit_rate (unique requests where prefix KV was reused) and byte-savings-per-minute (tokens avoided). also track tail-latency percentiles for cold vs warm. we can provide a recommended Grafana dashboard template — will share link to a sample dashboard and a CSV export from the POC run.
[38:00] Marissa: multi-tenant scheduling — if we shard caches per-gpu or per-pool, how do you avoid hot-tenant thrash?

[40:00] Carlos: use tenant-aware sharding and admission control. e.g., assign hot tenants to dedicated subset or enforce per-tenant eviction quotas. admission policies can route high-traffic tenants to dedicated pools where their cache and KV footprint is pinned.
[42:00] Ravi: for VPC/on-prem deployments, what changes? we have stricter network boundaries and internal KMS.

[44:00] Priya: on-prem we typically do per-tenant namespaces with HSM/KMS-managed keys. we also recommend running the cache as a local process (not cross-host) to reduce egress of KV blobs; or use a private memcached/redis inside the VPC with TLS and auth. Redwood can provide config templates for VPC deployment and KMS integration — we'll attach those docs.
[46:00] Marissa: did you run any microbenchmarks showing cost impact — tokens saved vs memory overhead?

[48:00] Priya: quick example from a recent POC: prefix caching reduced per-request GPU token compute by ~42% and reduced 95th latency from 220ms cold to 90ms warm at 60% hit; memory overhead was about 1.8GB per 100k hot prefixes using an optimized kv layout. results vary by prefix length distribution and model size.
[50:00] Liam: great — next steps and recap please, and security asks from Ravi.

[52:00] Jared: recap — action items below. we'll follow-up with a POC plan: Redwood to run a controlled benchmark on Verdant staging using their sample traffic, send recommended cache config, security design doc for per-tenant isolation and KMS patterns. thanks everyone.
